data: Variant groups, calmer search, code-signed installs

Group alternate versions of an asset under a single entry, get a gentle nudge to update, and enjoy a search that stays out of your way until you want it. Plus new file types, sturdier 3D models, hardened archive handling, and code-signed Windows installers.

A new way to group variations of an asset, more file types, a friendlier updater, and a search index that waits for your say-so. Plus tidier watched-folder imports and sturdier 3D models.

🔗 Link assets as alternates with variant groups

Sometimes several files are really one asset: frames of an animation, or a 3D model exported to different formats. Variant groups fold them into a single entry, without touching the files on disk.

  • A brand-new way to group alternate versions of an asset (different resolutions, colourways, formats) under a single entry, so your library stays tidy instead of cluttered with near-duplicates.
  • Variant groups fan out inline, so you can expand a group and see every member without leaving the view.
  • Groups carry their own icon and an accurate member count everywhere they appear, including the Workbench and Projects, where adding a group reads "add N items to project" rather than counting as one.

📦 More file types supported

  • Affinity Photo files (.afphoto) now import with thumbnails and metadata.
  • Piskel sprites (.piskel) are recognised, with an animated preview so you can watch the sprite play.
  • Clip Studio Paint files (.clip) now show thumbnails and metadata.

🔄 A smoother update experience

  • AssetHoard now tells you when a new release is available, with one-click options to install it, read the notes, or skip for now.
  • Returning users now see the "What's New" notes on upgrade, instead of the first-run Welcome screen.

🔍 Calmer, more reliable search

  • Search indexing no longer kicks off automatically at startup. Instead you get a gentle prompt to start it when you want, so launching the app stays fast and light.
  • Fixed Mac indexing that couldn't be cancelled once it started.
  • If a search model is corrupted, AssetHoard now spots it at boot and offers to re-download it.
  • Indexing large libraries is faster thanks to a more efficient matching pass.

📥 Tidier watched-folder imports

A few bug fixes this release to make the watched-folder experience smoother

  • Fixed a white screen on boot that could happen while watched folders were being scanned.
  • Folders that have already settled no longer re-import every time you open the app.
  • Re-importing a folder no longer leaves behind duplicate, often-empty bundles.
  • Boot scans are quicker with a single-pass walk over your watched folders.

📐 Better 3D models

  • 3D model metadata is now normalised and presented consistently across formats.
  • Missing OBJ materials (.mtl) no longer spam errors into the view and logs. They're listed in the asset's Resources panel in the sidebar instead, so you can see what's missing without the noise.
  • General speed improvements to 3D model loading.

🔒 Security and hardening

  • Gated database-reset command behind a system prompt.
  • Hardened archive extraction (tar and 7z) against malicious paths explosion attacks.
  • Added protection against malicious oversized images across all file types.
  • Windows installers are now code-signed, so you'll see fewer security warnings on install.

🐛 Polish and fixes

  • Added an "Open Log Directory" button in Settings > Data to make sharing diagnostics easier.
  • Upgraded audio decoding for broader format coverage and reliability.

Happy hoarding.
Dependency tracking, richer bundles, lighter search

See what your 3D models and materials depend on, flatten and organise bundles more freely, and reclaim around 450 MB by turning search off. Plus new file types, separate audio channels, and a steadier importer.

New file types, a clear view of what your 3D models and materials depend on, richer bundles, and a search index that is lighter on memory. Plus a stack of polish and fixes.

📦 More file types supported

  • Tiled maps (.tmx) now show up with proper thumbnails and a live preview, so your level maps look like everything else in your library.
  • Paint.NET files (.pdn) are now recognised and imported.

🔗 See what your 3D models and materials depend on

  • Selecting a 3D model (OBJ, GLTF/GLB) or material (MTL) now reveals its associated files, grouped into three clear lists: in your library, on disk but not imported, and missing.
  • OBJ models flatten their .mtl and the textures it pulls in into a single list, so you can answer "are my textures here?" at a glance.
  • The missing group is expanded by default, making it easy to diagnose why a preview looks untextured, and every entry has a reveal-in-folder action.
  • The "on disk, not imported" group keeps a one-click import action. The same wording now applies to Godot .tres references too.

🗂 Better bundles and organisation

  • A new "Show all" toggle lets you flatten a bundle and view every asset inside it at once, including those tucked away in nested bundles, without changing how anything is stored.
  • Categories now flow through bundles. A category set on a bundle is reflected on the bundle and the assets within it, and categories show up directly in the tree and on asset rows as tags.
  • Bundle summaries are richer, showing the file types contained inside at a glance.
  • Projects, tags and categories can now all be managed from the Settings menu, giving you one place to tidy up your library.
  • Drag onto breadcrumbs to move items up the hierarchy. Drop assets, bundles, or a mixed selection onto any ancestor breadcrumb to move them in one gesture, without hunting for the target in the sidebar tree. Works in the library, workbench and project views.
  • Right-click menus on bundles are now consistent wherever you use them.
  • Bundle previews are noticeably faster, especially for bundles with lots of tagged assets.

🔊 Smoother audio

  • Audio previews now show separate left and right channel waveforms.
  • Hitting play now properly selects and previews the track.
  • 🐛 Track length and file size display correctly in list view.

📥 A more reliable import experience

  • Import progress now moves steadily forward instead of jumping around.
  • 🐛 Fixed a problem where watched-folder imports could appear to get stuck and never finish.

🔍 Faster, lighter search

  • Turning search off now frees up around 450 MB of memory and can be cancelled at any time, with indexes kept on disk so switching it back on is quick.
  • Search indexing is smarter and lighter, updating as you add assets rather than rebuilding from scratch, so large imports feel snappier.

🐛 Polish and fixes

  • Added a "Re-detect Pixel Art" button in Settings > Data that re-runs render-profile auto-detection across your library, so you can fix renderers that look wrong without re-importing. Your manual choices, bundle defaults and category defaults are preserved, and it runs in the background with a cancellable progress bar.
  • Fixed a Unity-related settings issue and improved the empty-state experience in settings (it no longer errors on certain operating systems).
  • Thumbnails now fit cleanly without being clipped.
  • Added protection against malicious oversized images.
  • Various stability fixes for Blender packages and previews.
  • Project descriptions are now editable in the header to match bundles.
  • Semantic Search never ceasing to intialise at startup is now been fixed

Happy hoarding.
A quick Ctrl+P palette, animated variants, and a tidier window
A streamlined toolbar, a collapsible sidebar, and a new Ctrl+P command palette to jump anywhere instantly. Plus smarter image search and animated variants.

A cleaner window, a faster way to get around, and image search that reaches more of your library. Plus bulk edits for tags and categories, animated variant groups, and calmer imports.

⌨️ Jump anywhere with Ctrl+P

A new quick palette lets you press Ctrl+P and jump straight to any bundle, asset, project or command

Here's how to drive it:

  • Just start typing to search across your bundles, assets and projects at once. The closest hit is lifted to the top as the best match, and any commands that fit come along too.
  • Type > to switch to command mode, where you can import, create a new bundle, flip view options, change theme, open settings and more.
  • Narrow things down with a scope: @bundles, @assets or @projects searches only that kind. Add a query after it to keep going, such as @assets tree.

🎞 Animated variant groups

  • Variant groups can now play their frames in sequence as an animation.
  • Drag frames to set the order.

🪟 Redesigned header & toolbar

  • We've retired the old title bar in favour of a streamlined toolbar, with sort and view options now sitting together in the search header.
  • The import button has moved somewhere more sensible, and everything lines up better.
  • Need more room? You can now collapse the left sidebar to give your assets centre stage.
  • On Linux, you can now choose how window controls appear: all buttons, close only, or your OS defaults.
  • Mac window buttons now sit where they should.

🗂 Bulk tidy-ups for tags and categories

  • Select multiple tags or categories to merge or remove them in one go, right from settings.
  • Changed your mind? It's all undoable.

🔍 Smarter image search

  • Improved image indexing means more of your images turn up in semantic search.
  • A single corrupt or mislabelled image no longer stops the whole indexing run.
  • Broken images are quietly set aside instead of nagging you as "still pending" forever.

🐛 Polish, fixes, and formats

  • TIFF files are now supported.
  • A new setting lets you choose how thumbnails fit their frame, Fit or Fill.
  • Your sort order is now remembered between restarts.
  • Tidier keyboard-shortcuts and import screens.
  • A handful of behind-the-scenes stability improvements.
  • Set how many imports run at once to match your machine.
  • When you remove items from a bundle, we'll now tell you which projects are affected first.
  • Created a project, bundle, and workbench default sidebar panel view to make the sidebar contextual to the current position in the library

Happy hoarding.
